newsitem.title: USA: Limit-up soybeans, cash strength rally CBOT meal.
newsitem.headline: Limit-up soybeans, cash strength rally CBOT meal.

text.p: Limit-up gains in soybean futures and strength in cash basis levels spurred strong advances in CBOT soymeal futures at midsession Friday, floor traders said.
Soyoil futures were also higher, but advances were limited by lackluster dealings in U.S. cash and export markets, floor sources said.
Concerns about scant old-crop soybean ending stocks and technical strength pushed nearby soybean contracts sharply higher Friday.
Cash soymeal traders reported rail basis offers were $1.00 to $3.00 per ton higher because of tight soybean supplies.
An strong weekly crushing pace of 25.378 million bushels for the week ended June 11 was also seen dampening buying enthusiasm in soyoil, traders said.
In early soymeal trade, Cargill and Goldenberg Hehmeyer each bought 200 lots of July. In the soyoil pit, Cargill also bought 200 lots of July, traders said.
CBOT July soymeal was $6.00 per ton higher at $282.70 and other months were $1.80 to $4.10 higher. July soyoil was up 0.06 cent a lb at 23.30 and other months were 0.03 to 0.13 cent higher.
